title.text: This is LucentDock, a smart dock for Windows, built and verified in public.

problem_now.text: A normal taskbar remembers what you pinned. It misses what needs you now: the next meeting, a dying battery, or a limit you chose.

problem_context.text: Important context stays scattered across calendars, menus, notifications, and windows you must hunt down.

meeting_before.text: Ten minutes before design review, the everyday dock still carries media, weather, screen time, and the usual apps.

meeting_change.text: Then it rearranges itself. The calendar moves forward, leisure widgets step away, and the bar settles without covering your work.

undo.text: The change is an overlay, never a rewrite. Activity explains the rule and its reason, while one action restores the everyday dock.

groups_one.text: Six ideas cover the product: apps to arrange, fourteen useful widgets, and nine automations that respond to your day.

groups_two.text: Three styles join safety that fails visible and privacy by default: no account, no telemetry, and fixture data in public previews.

styles.text: Choose glass, dark, or liquid glass, where your own wallpaper bends at the rim through a lens instead of a generic blur.

proof_tests.text: Six hundred eighty two automated tests and reproducible build verification make each release artifact comparable byte for byte.

proof_gates.text: Attended owner gates at five display scales, independent audits, and explicit signoff come before installation.

role.text: Leonel Cortés coordinates the artificial intelligence systems. One implements, another audits blind, findings return to the builder, and only Leonel runs the final gate.

result.text: The first release is being prepared. Until then, build from source, inspect the evidence, verify the artifact hash, and remember that every dock change can be undone.
